I would keep doing what fits Quzhou best: a `winter wheat -> summer maize` rotation on the same land. In Quzhou, that is still the main grain system, and official and research sources describe the county as a typical North China Plain wheat-maize area, with most rain falling in the summer maize season and most irrigation pressure falling on winter wheat. Recent Quzhou “吨半粮” work also shows this same path, using improved wheat and high-yield maize, straw return, and integrated water-fertilizer management. So I would not switch into cotton or other labor-heavy cash crops. At 73, with middle-school education, I would choose the familiar system that is easy to organize with machines, easier to sell, and less risky for me to manage year to year. Sources I’m relying on: [PMC study on Quzhou cropping system](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/), [MOA / Hebei report on Quzhou wheat area](https://www.moa.gov.cn/ztzl/wcbgclz/qglb/202305/t20230522_6428066.htm), [Hebei/Quzhou “绿色吨半粮” report](https://www.agri.cn/zx/xxlb/hb/202410/t20241011_8677909.htm), [MOA wheat fertilization guidance](https://www.moa.gov.cn/gk/nszd_1/2023/202309/t20230928_6437567.htm), and [Hebei maize fertilization guidance summary](https://nyncj.chengde.gov.cn/art/2012/7/9/art_667_93731.html).

I would keep the plan simple. I would use improved winter wheat seed in autumn, plough after straw return so the soil layer stays deeper and holds water better, and give wheat two irrigations because in my area wheat depends on irrigation more than maize. I would not push fertilizer to the top end because I am old, I want stable yield rather than chasing extreme output, and Quzhou’s recent work shows better efficiency matters. After wheat harvest, I would sow hybrid summer maize directly or with very light tillage so I save labor and catch moisture fast. For maize I would usually irrigate once if the summer turns dry, otherwise let rainfall do most of the work. I would spray enough to control weeds, rust, aphids, and corn borer, but not more than needed. My goal would be steady grain income, manageable field work, and lower risk.
